MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic monofilament windshield nets.
requirements: Every roll or bundle of certified windshield net must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 17356) printed on a secure label or edge tape.

Windshield nets must be manufactured from high-quality HDPE monofilament yarns conforming to Clauses 4.1 and 4.1.1 of IS 17356:2020. The monofilament yarn shall be thoroughly UV-stabilised (for a minimum of 3 years resistance) and contain non-toxic pigments.
The fabric used in the manufacture of windshield nets shall be knitted on warp knitting machines and shall have a width as per the agreement between the buyer and the seller.
The standard classifies windshield nets into two primary types: Type 1 and Type 2. Separate samples of each type must be tested for scope certification.

Windshield nets must be provided with eyelets (or brass sail type eyelets conforming to IS 4084) along the length and width of the fabric as shown in Fig. 1 to facilitate secure installation. Typical edge-to-edge distances, eyelet-to-eyelet distances, and eyelet lengths must be declared.
Applicable for coloured windshield nets only. The colour fastness to artificial light must achieve a rating of 4 or better when evaluated using Xenon arc fading lamp test methods as per ISO 105-B02.

Windshield nets must resist severe localized forces. The bursting pressure of the fabric must be at least 10 kgf/cm² for Type 1 and 14 kgf/cm² for Type 2, evaluated as per hydraulic or pneumatic methods of IS 1966.

The primary aerodynamic purpose of the net is wind reduction. The wind blockage must be at least 18 percent for Type 1 and 35 percent for Type 2, tested as per the blower and measurement chamber method outlined in Annex C.

To guarantee durability under intense sun, the fabric must undergo accelerated UV weathering. The retained breaking strength (warpway and weftway) must be at least 85 percent of the original actual fabric strength, tested per Annex B and IS 1969 (Part 1).

Finished netting rolls must be clean, flat, uniform, and free from manufacturing defects such as missing yarns, distorted meshes, or scale. Colour or pigment mixture shall conform to sealed client reference samples.

For quality audit inspections, random samples must be selected per Table 2 (Scale of Sampling). Lots are defined as monofilament windshield net rolls/bundles of the same construction and type dispatched under one dispatch note.

requirements: Every roll or bundle of conforming geomembranes must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

The minimum thickness of the finished geomembrane must strictly comply with the variety: Type I: Min 0.25 mm; Type II: Min 0.50 mm; Type III: Min 0.75 mm; and Type IV: Min 1.00 mm, tested per IS 7016 (Part 1/Sec 3).

The minimum mass of the finished geomembrane must satisfy the specified limits: Type I: Min 250 g/m²; Type II: Min 420 g/m²; Type III: Min 650 g/m²; and Type IV: Min 950 g/m², tested per IS 7016 (Part 1/Sec 2).
The polymer coating must contain a minimum of 2.5 percent carbon black by mass to provide superior UV light stabilization and durability during outdoor weathering, tested per IS 2530.

Puncture resistance is evaluated by clamping a specimen without tension between plates of a ring clamp with an open internal diameter of 45 mm ± 0.025 mm [2, 4]. A solid steel rod (diameter 7.92 mm ± 0.25 mm) with a flat chisel-shaped tip (thickness 0.8 mm ± 0.1 mm, tip edges rounded to 0.25 mm radius) is oriented at 45° to intercept warp and weft threads [5]. The test is executed at a machine speed of 300 mm/min ± 10 mm/min until rupture [3]. The maximum force recorded is reported as puncture resistance [2].

Prior to testing puncture resistance, specimens must be conditioned in a controlled atmosphere of 65 percent ± 5 percent relative humidity and 27 °C ± 2 °C temperature until moisture equilibrium is reached, which is defined as mass increase <= 0.1% over successive weighings spaced >= 2 h apart.

To determine ash content and verify polymer purity, the muffle furnace must be calibrated and operated at a corrected high temperature of 590 °C (correcting the older limit of 550 °C). The test sample mass is strictly restricted to 3 g ± 0.2 g (previously 30 g ± 2 g) to ensure complete thermal digestion of organic remains.

The finished geomembrane must exhibit zero water leakage when subjected to hydrostatic pressure testing, and the heat-welded joints must maintain high seam strengths both before and after prolonged UV exposure.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Protective Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (including the Quality Control Amendment Order, 2024) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all textile-based curtains and drapes intended for use in public, residential, or institutional interiors must conform to IS 15741:2007 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India. Products manufactured solely for export are exempt if they conform to foreign buyers' specifications. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial technical textiles or fire-resistant drapes.
requirements: Every roll or prefabricated piece of curtains and drapes conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Curtains or drapes must satisfy specified ignition-resistance thresholds given in Table 1 when tested against defined categories of hazardous public places/buildings as specified in Annex B. Other quality requirements must satisfy relevant Indian Standards or be mutually agreed upon.

The flame-retardant properties of the curtains, drapes, or their fabrics must remain fully effective, satisfying specified ignitability limits after undergoing a minimum of 50 laundering cycles as per the standard washing procedure (Clause C-5) or reduced washing procedure (Clause C-6).

During laundering, ballast consisting of single-layer rectangular pieces of woven 100 percent bleached cotton or 100 percent polyester must be added. Each piece must measure at least 350 × 500 mm and be hemmed along the cut edges to prevent unravelling.

Preliminary laundering calculations require specific machine settings. Type A1 machines: drum volume 70 L, dry test load mass 4.2 ± 0.3 kg, low dip volume 21.0 ± 1.5 L, high dip volume 38.0 ± 3.0 L, and detergent mass 21.0 ± 1.5 g. Type A2 machines: drum volume 45 L, dry test load mass 2.7 ± 0.2 kg, low dip volume 13.5 ± 1.0 L, high dip volume 24.5 ± 2.0 L, and detergent mass 13.5 ± 1.0 g.

Load the machine to computed test load mass (m1) with soft water to low dip level (L) at 15 °C to 40 °C, and add low-foaming reference detergent (m2) mixed with perborate immediately before use (1 part perborate to 4 parts detergent). If the inlet water is below 37 °C, heat to 40±3 °C with no agitation, then heat to 75±3 °C in 15±3 min with reduced agitation. Run at 75±3 °C for 15±0.5 min with normal agitation and drain. Fill with cold soft water to high dip level (H), run for 3 min, and drain; repeat this rinsing sequence three more times (total of four rinses). Centrifuge for 6 min. This entire wash-rinse-centrifuge cycle must be repeated 49 times to achieve a total of 50 complete cycles.
The Toxicity Index of gases evolved during the complete burning of 100 g of curtains, drapes, or their fabrics must be a maximum of 1.0.

The toxicity index is a numerical summation of the toxicity factors of selected gases produced by complete combustion under flaming conditions in excess air inside an airtight chamber of at least 1 m³ (approximately 100 × 100 × 100 cm³) lined with opaque plastic. The summation factors are derived based on each gas concentration fatal to man in a 30-minute exposure time. A total index of 1.0, on average, brings about death in 30 minutes.

The mathematical toxicity calculations utilize the following specific fatal exposure levels (in ppm) to determine individual gas factors: Carbon dioxide (100,000 ppm), Carbon monoxide (4,000 ppm), Hydrogen sulphide (750 ppm), Ammonia (750 ppm), Formaldehyde (500 ppm), Hydrogen chloride (500 ppm), Acrylonitrile (400 ppm), Sulphur dioxide (400 ppm), Nitrogen oxides (250 ppm), Phenol (250 ppm), Hydrogen cyanide (150 ppm), Hydrogen bromide (150 ppm), Hydrogen fluoride (100 ppm), and Phosgene (25 ppm).

Testing must be conducted at an air temperature of 27 ± 2 °C. Fabric specimens (normally 3) must be cut to sizes that will be entirely engulfed in the flame. Test pieces are suspended over a Bunsen burner (125 mm overall height, 11 mm bore burner tube, and 5 mm bore gas and air inlet tubes) established at a flow rate of 10 L/min gas and 15 L/min air. The burner is ignited and extinguished from outside using a separate small pin flame. The specimen is subjected to a calibrated flaming temperature of 1150 ± 50 °C. To prevent sample losses from melting or dripping, specimens can be supported on a thin bed of glass wool placed over the wire support mesh.

All rolls, pieces, or curtains of identical type manufactured under similar conditions and supplied against a single dispatch note constitute a lot. Random samples must be selected as per col 2 and col 3 of Table 2 to test for ignitability and laundering durability. All samples must meet specified parameters for the lot to be declared conforming.

requirements: Every roll or bundle of PVC geomembranes conforming to the quality and performance requirements of this standard must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L) [4].

If two or more layers of PVC films are combined to achieve the target thickness, they must be joined strictly using heat fusion lamination [10]. Joining layers using adhesives is explicitly prohibited [10]. For constructing larger panels, sheets must be joined by heat-sealing with a minimum overlap of 2.5 cm [11].

The geomembranes are classified into two categories based on end-use: Category A (Type I: 0.30 mm, Type II: 0.50 mm, Type III: 0.75 mm, Type IV: 1.00 mm, and Type V: 1.50 mm nominal thickness) [11] and Category B (Type VI: 2.00 mm, Type VII: 2.50 mm, and Type VIII: 3.00 mm nominal thickness) [5].

To determine consignment conformity, representative sample rolls must be drawn randomly based on lot size: up to 50 rolls (select 3, permissible defectives = 0); 51 to 150 rolls (select 5, permissible defectives = 0); 151 to 300 rolls (select 8, permissible defectives = 0); and 301 and above (select 13, permissible defectives = 0) [6].

Dumbbell-shaped test specimens (5 longitudinal and 5 transverse) must be prepared [12]. Prior to testing, they must be conditioned for at least 20 hours at 27 ± 2 °C and 65 ± 5% relative humidity [12]. Tensile testing must run at a grip separation speed of 100 ± 10 mm/min [12]. Category B grades must satisfy a minimum longitudinal and transverse tensile strength of 17 N/mm² [5].

Tear resistance must be tested using a constant rate of grip separation machine on specimens cut with a die [13, 14]. The tear propagation strength is calculated using the formula: TS = L/t, where TS is tear propagation strength, L is maximum force (N), and t is the average specimen thickness (mm) [15].

Six random specimens (50 mm wide, 225 mm long) must be conditioned in a chamber at the specified sub-zero test temperature for at least 60 minutes alongside a 40 mm diameter mandrel [16, 17]. The test piece is manually bent 180° over the mandrel in approximately 3 seconds [17]. The bent surface is evaluated under 4X magnification and must show zero cracks, breaks, or failures [17].

Specimens must be exposed to ultraviolet light in a Xenon-arc apparatus for 500 hours under 120-minute cycles (102 minutes light only, followed by 18 minutes water spray + light) [18]. Post-exposure tensile strength and elongation are compared against unexposed values to assess weathering degradation [18].

For high-pressure structural uses, a specimen (conditioned for 20 hours at standard atmosphere) is placed with its upper side downwards in a water-filled apparatus against a standardized slotted plate [3, 19]. A hydrostatic test pressure of 5 bar must be applied continuously for 24 hours at 27 ± 2 °C and 65 ± 5% RH, and the sample must remain completely watertight [19].

Specimens must be suspended vertically in an oven at 70 °C for 2 hours [21]. The displacement/change in dimensions is measured, and a mean change greater than 2.0 mm constitutes a dimensional stability failure [21].

During installation, a layer of soft soil must be applied, and the subgrade and slopes must be compacted to at least 90 percent of proctor density up to a depth of 300 mm to provide solid support for the geomembrane [22]. Anchor trenches (typically 500 mm x 500 mm) must secure the edges of the liner [23, 24].

To prevent damage to the liner, shade nets must be installed over the geomembrane at the corners of ponds or reservoirs, providing crawling friction so trapped reptiles can escape instead of clawing and tearing the sheet [23, 24].

Under Amendment No. 1, to evaluate moisture-retention capability, the water holding capacity must be tested as per Annex C and calculated using the corrected formula:

All constituent materials (outer shell, moisture barrier, thermal barrier) must withstand hot air exposure at 180°C for 5 minutes, showing zero ignition, melting, or dripping, and maximum dimensional shrinkage must not exceed 5 percent.

The moisture barrier must resist chemical penetration (sulfuric acid, sodium hydroxide, o-xylene) under pressure, and the outer shell must satisfy high water-repellency ratings (spray rating >= 4).

Each item must be legibly and indelibly marked with: manufacturer's name/brand, standard number (IS 16890), category (Category 1 or Category 2), size designation (girth/height), batch/lot number, fiber composition, and extensive washing/drying care instructions.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Medical Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all reusable sanitary pads, sanitary napkins, and period panties manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 17514 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified reusable menstrual products in India is a punishable offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Micro and small enterprises are granted specific delayed implementation phases, and products manufactured by Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to technical and medical textile products.
requirements: Every commercial pack of reusable sanitary pads/napkins/period panties must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to verify conformity.

The composite product must consist of three primary layers to ensure moisture absorption and isolation: a) top cover or top sheet (for skin contact comfort); b) absorbent core (middle layer featuring highly absorbent woven/non-woven fabrics to retain fluid); and c) barrier or bottom layer (leak-proof backing layer to prevent fluid pass-through to outer garments).

The raw fabrics used for manufacturing must satisfy minimum colorfastness limits (to washing, rubbing, and acidic/alkaline perspiration) and show zero excessive shrinkage or elongation (dimensional stability to washing) as specified in Table 1.
The pH of the cold aqueous extract of the product must lie within a safe skin-compatible range when evaluated in accordance with IS 1390.

The product must absorb standard volumes of colored distilled water (defined by size and capacity) and withstand a 1 kg standard load applied for 1 minute as per Annex B without showing any side or bottom leakage.

To prevent bacterial and fungal growth during repeated use, the total viable microbial count (bioburden) must not exceed 1 000 cfu/gm when tested per ISO 11737 (Part 1). Pathogenic Staphylococcus aureus must be completely absent when evaluated per IS 5887 (Part 2).

Under Amendment No. 3, to protect users from hormone-disrupting chemicals, the total individual or combined phthalate plasticizer levels in raw materials or finished products must be less than 0.1 percent when tested in accordance with IS 9873 (Part 6) at least once a year.

If required by the buyer, the raw materials must undergo biocompatibility evaluations (cytotoxicity, irritation, and skin sensitization tests under IS/ISO 10993 and IS 17932). If antibacterial properties are claimed, the fabric must demonstrate an antibacterial activity value of 2 or more initially and after the declared wash cycles when evaluated per IS/ISO 20743.

Grouped by identical materials, sizes, and manufacturing batches, random samples must be drawn per Table 2 for non-destructive and destructive testing to audit workmanship and absorption safety prior to lot acceptance.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Medical Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all medical bedsheets and pillow covers (disposable or reusable) manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 17630:2021 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified hospital bedding is a criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to healthcare bedsheets and pillow covers.
requirements: Every commercial pack of bedsheets and pillow covers conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to certify compliance.
Bedsheets and pillow covers must be manufactured from spunlace and/or spunbond non-woven fabric, or woven fabric; made of cotton, polyester, or their blends.
Products are classified as: a) Single Use (Disposable); b) Reusable. If reusable, the manufacturer must declare the maximum wash cycles / life cycle of the product.

The manufacture and preparation of the bedsheets and pillow covers must be conducted under proper hygienic conditions. The manufacturer must implement and record a systematic factory hygiene maintenance program.
The finished products must be clean and free from lumping, holes, tears, or chemicals/substances that can cause tendering or degradation during storage.

To prevent tearing or splitting during patient handling, the fabric must satisfy strict minimum mechanical limits on: a) Tensile strength (dry and wet) tested per IS 15891 (Part 3) or IS 1969 (Part 1); b) Bursting strength (dry and wet) tested per IS 1966 (Part 1); c) Seam strength (dry and wet) to verify stitch robustness.

Fabric dyes must show high stability against clinical exposure, satisfying specified limits on: colorfastness to rubbing (dry and wet), colorfastness to perspiration (acidic and alkaline), colorfastness to light, and colorfastness to washing.
The pH of the cold aqueous extract of the material must be strictly verified as skin-friendly when tested in accordance with IS 1390.

To maintain hygiene in sterile environments, the total viable microbial count (bacterial and fungal bioburden) must satisfy strict limits when tested as per the dilution and plating out methods of ISO 11737-1.
The fabric must show low linting and low particle release properties under standard dynamic testing to prevent aerosol contamination of sterile clinical spaces.

Under Amendment No. 2, the biocompatibility evaluation is optional. If specified by the purchaser, the raw material must pass in-vitro cytotoxicity testing per IS/ISO 10993 (Part 5) with a result of 'non-cytotoxic', and pass irritation and skin sensitization tests.
The fabric must limit water-soluble chemicals to prevent leaching or chemical contact with patients.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (Agrotech QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all HDPE laminated woven lay flat tubes and fittings supplied for rain irrigation systems must conform to IS 17728:2021 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified rain pipes in India is a statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic irrigation piping systems.
requirements: Each dispatched bundle or roll of lay flat tube must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 17728).

Tapes used in weaving the fabric must be manufactured from UV-stabilized high-density polyethylene granules. If carbon black is added, it must contain a minimum of 2.5 percent of carbon black by mass with satisfactory dispersion tested per IS 2530. The tape width must be at least 2.0 mm, and linear density must be at least 77.7 Tex (700 Denier).

The manufacturer must declare the range of working pressure between the minimum working pressure (Pmin) and maximum working pressure (Pmax) within which the perforated lay flat tube operates effectively.
The woven lay flat tube fabric must demonstrate high breaking strength. Average breaking strength in N must be determined under standard crosshead traverse speeds of 300 ± 15 mm/min.

The fabric must resist physical puncture. Average puncture resistance must be calculated from 5 tested specimens clamped in a circular ring clamp (grooved with an O-ring or sandpaper) using a solid steel rod plunge attached to a load indicator.
The lay flat tube specimen must pass bending tests without physical cracking. It passes if none of the first 10 bends fails, or not more than 2 fail in a total sample of 20 bends.

To prevent orifice tearing or warping under severe summer sun, hot water is circulated through a 1-meter sample at maximum working pressure (Pmax). The percentage change in hole diameter must be less than 5 percent.

Water flow rate is measured in litres per hour per metre (l/h/m) across the declared working pressure range (Pmin, Pnom, Pmax). Flow rates for nominal diameters—including standard sizes 32 mm and 40 mm—must stay within ±5 percent of the manufacturer's declared value.

Under nominal working pressure, a 40 m length (for 32 mm size) or 45 m length (for 40 mm size) lay flat tube is tested on flat ground. The farthest spray throw distance must meet specified agricultural irrigation bounds.

A standard commercial rain pipe kit consists of: a) Main/Sub-main line (IS 16627); b) Perforated lay flat tube; c) Pump-to-main line connectors; d) Sub-main-to-lay flat tube connectors; e) Tube-to-tube jointers.
Prior to storage, the entire system must be dried completely. The lay flat tube must be stored securely to prevent structural damage from rodents.

The sub-main line is branched using metal or plastic TEEs based on internal diameter (e.g. 75mm x 63mm for a 75mm main). Hoses are secured on connectors up to the rubber flat ring and tightened with clamps to guarantee no leakage.
For assembly, the lock ring must be pulled forward, the rain pipe put on the start connector, and the ring pulled backward towards the rain pipe properly to ensure no leakage.

Under the 'Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (Agrotech QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all Laminated Woven Orchard Protection Covers manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 17731:2021 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified orchard covers in the Indian market is a statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic woven laminates.
requirements: Every commercial roll or pack of orchard protection cover must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 17731) on a secure label or edge tape.

Orchard protection covers are constructed from high-quality High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) woven fabrics laminated with Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE) and fortified with specialized UV-stabilized additives to resist weathering and sun-bleaching.

Woven laminated covers are commonly produced in standard weights such as 140 GSM (g/m²) and 160 GSM, as declared by the manufacturer. Mass tolerances must stay within strictly bounded limits to ensure uniform material density.
To guarantee thermal insulation and physical barrier durability, the thickness of the laminated sheet must meet specified minimum values (mm, Min).

The cover must withstand wind shear and hailstorm forces. Average warpway and weftway breaking strength must be tested as per the strip method of IS 1969 (Part 1) and exceed specified minimum thresholds (N, Min).

To ensure long-term outdoor field performance (expected 4 to 5 years service life), the fabric must undergo 1000 hours of accelerated UV weathering and retain a high percentage of its original actual breaking strength (percent, Min).
The fabric must show controlled elasticity to absorb physical impacts. Elongation/strain limits (percent) are strictly evaluated at peak breaking load.

The cover must resist falling hail and heavy rain. It must meet a specified minimum impact failure load when evaluated at a standard 1524 mm drop height (expressed as gram force at 50 percent failure).
For Type II covers, the integrated reinforced band must exhibit outstanding tensile strength (N, Min) to handle tight rope-tying and anchoring on support structures.
To prevent excessive inorganic fillers that degrade polymer performance, the ash content of the material is limited to a strict maximum percentage (percent, Max).

To maintain optimal horticultural growth conditions and prevent excessive heat buildup, the cover must satisfy specified total visible light transmission parameters (percent) to diffuse direct summer sun.

For secure installations, the covers are loosely placed on support frames and secured using brass or synthetic eyelets along the reinforced edges, allowing them to be tied tightly with flexible ropes.

certification.description: Voluntary / Statutory. Conformance with IS 5405 ensures compliance with hygiene, biocompatibility, and absorption standards. Products conforming to this standard are certified under Scheme-I and may be marked with the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards in accordance with the BIS Act, 2016. Hallmarking is completely inapplicable to technical and medical textile products.
requirements: Every product complying with this standard may be certified under BIS Scheme-I and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence along with the registered licence number (CM/L).
Disposable sanitary napkins, panty liners, maternity pads, and period panties basically consist of three main layers: a) cover or top sheet; b) absorbent core; and c) barrier or bottom sheet.

The cover or top sheet coming into contact with the skin must be of good quality cotton, rayon knitted sleeve, gauze, non-woven fabric, or other porous materials. If cotton gauze is used, it must conform to IS 758.

The absorbent core forming the middle layer must consist of filler materials such as cellulose pulp, cellulose wadding, tissue, cotton, wood pulp, or super absorbent materials. It must be free from unintended lumps, oil spots, dirt, or foreign matter that can cause skin injury or discomfort.
The barrier or bottom sheet must be made of suitable leak-proof material to prevent fluid pass-through, satisfying the pressure-resistance requirements after absorption.
The pH of the aqueous extract of the product must lie within the range of 3.5 to 7.5 when evaluated in accordance with IS 1390.

The products must absorb colored distilled water (tested per Annex B at 27 ± 2 °C) and withstand a 1 kg standard weight applied for 1 minute on the wet portion without showing any bottom or side leakage. The minimum fluid absorption values are: a) Sanitary Napkin: 30 ml; b) Panty Liner: 1 ml; c) Maternity Pad: 50 ml; d) Period Panty: 30 ml.

To prevent biological contamination and infection, the total viable microbial count (bacteria and fungi) must not exceed 1 000 cfu/gm. Pathogenic Staphylococcus aureus must be completely absent when evaluated per Clause 7.3.2.1.

The products must be produced under good hygienic conditions in accordance with the Good Manufacturing Practice guidelines outlined in Annex C (including separate demarcated storage, 70% Isopropyl Alcohol hand sanitizers, proper lighting, ventilation, and pest control).

If specified by the buyer, raw materials must be tested and show reactivity as 'non-cytotoxic' under IS/ISO 10993-5, and be 'Non-irritant and Non-sensitizer' when tested per IS 17932 (Part 7) and IS 17932 (Part 6) respectively.

The amount of phthalate present in the product must be less than 0.1 percent (individually or in combination) when tested at raw material stage or in the final product as per IS 9873 (Part 6) at least once a year.

If compostability is claimed, the product must pass IS/ISO 17088. If anti-bacterial activity is claimed, the raw or finished material must demonstrate an antibacterial activity value of 2 or more when evaluated as per the absorption method of IS/ISO 20743.

Each consumer pack must be legibly and indelibly marked with: manufacturer's name, size, type, quantity, directions of use, disposability instructions, batch/lot number, date of manufacture, and compostability/biocompatibility certifications (if applicable).

Finished products must be packed in rigid or flexible packages (such as carton board, PE, PP, or polyester) that protect against contaminants during shipment and storage. The packaging must be completely free of tears or damage.
